subject: ControlLink regression observed during rolling upgrade — OptiHealth private deployment
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Kelly <nora.kelly@optihealth.com>, OptiHealth Oncall <ops@optihealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ControlLink regression observed during rolling upgrade — OptiHealth private deployment

Hi Nora / OptiHealth ops team,

We observed a transient regression in the ControlLink connection layer while performing a scheduled rolling upgrade of the private control plane in your VPC this morning (upgrade window 08:30–09:00 PT). The symptoms:
- ~1–2 minute spike of orchestrator-control RPC timeouts for approx 5% of agents, which caused short-lived retries and a small increase in inference tail latency.
- Automatic failovers completed, no data-plane inference loss detected.

We've collated logs and traces and attached a support bundle (support_bundle_OptiHealth_20261102.tar.gz) that contains connection traces and orchestrator diagnostics. Initial root-cause hypothesis: an unexpected kernel selector fallback in the upgrade job caused a brief uptick in control-plane CPU in a subset of nodes, which triggered backoff behavior in the controllink heartbeat path.

Immediate actions we took:
- Rolled back the remaining hosts on the second batch to the previous stable image at 09:18 PT.
- Increased controllink keepalive rate for the affected nodes to expedite reconnection.
- Enabled more verbose connection tracing and uploaded the artifacts to the shared Drive link.

Next steps we propose:
1) Nightly artifact analysis and a follow-up bridge with your ops team to walk through traces (can do today at 17:00 PT).
2) A postmortem with timeline and code/packaging mitigation by Wednesday EOD.
3) A patch that forces deterministic kernel selection when upgrading, to be staged in our test environment tomorrow.

Please let me know if you want us to open a full incident bridge now. I’m standing by and will add Marissa and Priyom to lead remediation.

Thanks,
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Customer Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

Connor — thanks for the quick note and for the rollback. We saw a handful of elevated 5xx traces in our app logs around 09:10 PT but no customer-facing errors reported. Ops would like the bridge at 17:00 PT to review traces and the rollback plan.

Two asks from our side:
- Can you confirm whether KV-cache state could have been impacted for long-lived streams? We had a few long-chat sessions (50–60k tokens) during that interval and want to ensure no silent truncation.
- If there is a patch, can you provide an expected schedule and whether a maintenance window will be required?

Nora
Nora Kelly

Connor

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Kelly <nora.kelly@optihealth.com>, OptiHealth Oncall <ops@optihealth.com>

Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Follow-up: root cause & mitigations for ControlLink regression (OptiHealth)

Hi Nora / OptiHealth team — thanks again for the bridge earlier today. Below is a concise follow-up and the mitigations we will deploy.

Summary / timeline:
- 2026-11-02 08:30 PT: Rolling upgrade started (batched by AZ).
- 2026-11-02 09:07 PT: Kernel selector fallback observed on ctrl-host-7 and ctrl-host-9; brief CPU thrash followed.
- 2026-11-02 09:12–09:18 PT: ControlLink RTTs spiked for ~5% of agents; automatic retries and failovers kicked in.
- 2026-11-02 09:18 PT: Remaining batch rolled back; cluster stabilized; no persistent KV-cache divergence detected.

Root cause (short): during the upgrade we unintentionally allowed a non-deterministic kernel selection path in the control plane packaging step. In a small subset of hosts this triggered suboptimal kernel choices under load, increasing CPU and delaying heartbeats.

Impact: brief elevation in control-plane latency and a small window of increased inference tail latency for a minority of requests. No evidence of token loss or KV-cache truncation for long-lived sessions based on the trace scan we ran.

Mitigations and timeline:
- Immediate: rolled back second batch during the window (completed 11/02). Increased heartbeat frequency as a temporary backstop.
- Short-term (48–72 hrs): ship a safety patch that forces deterministic kernel selection during upgrade operations; will be gated by a feature-flag and released to private customers for staged rollout.
- Medium-term (2 weeks): add an upgrade preflight that simulates kernel selection on a canary host under sample load to detect selector regressions before batch rollouts.

Artifacts attached: controllink-trace-20261102.zip, support_bundle_OptiHealth_20261102.tar.gz. We also uploaded detailed timelines and raw traces to the Drive folder linked above and created RW-1187 for the engineering work.

Action items for OptiHealth:
- Optional: accept a short maintenance window for the safety patch (we recommend a low-traffic window; patch does not require data-plane downtime).
- Confirm whether you want us to run an extended KV-cache verification sweep on any sessions you identify as sensitive; we can prioritize.

If you'd like, we can provide a short one-page incident summary suitable for your compliance records.

Thanks for patience and the quick collaboration — we’ll keep you updated as the patch is staged.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Inference Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
